options.name: Calendar
options.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished mobile screen concept for the existing Cathopedia app, using the attached screenshot as visual style reference. This is a UI proposal, not a screenshot reproduction. Output ONE separate portrait image of ONE phone, centered, straight-on, subtle thin silver/black Android device frame with even outer margins, readable app content primary. Cross-platform premium neutral. Keep the established navy background #101d2c, Marian blue surfaces #073c70, warm gold #d9b634, cream text #eee9dc and muted powder blue #b5cce0. Refined serif titles, readable humanist sans labels, generous but practical spacing, radius 18-22 dp, fine blue-grey borders, no neon, no purple, no oversized charts, no promotional art, no invented rewards/streaks.
Show the Holy Rosary page at the statistics section. Header back arrow and centered serif "Holy Rosary". A compact "Resume my prayer" card, subtitle "Luminous mysteries · prayer 1", small gold open-book icon and chevron. Then a compact panel headed "Your Rosaries" with two equal numbers "2" and "2", labels "Completed" and "This month". Below redesign the original unlabeled blue boxes activity table using the specified variant. Lower section "By mystery set": Joyful 0, Sorrowful 2, Glorious 0, Luminous 0. Real sample data: only two completions, BOTH on Friday 9 October 2026, BOTH Sorrowful. Today Sunday 11 October 2026. No invented completed days. Distinguish completed day and today's outline clearly. Natural app controls and comfortably legible text. This is a calm devotional prayer history screen. Fit the activity design and breakdown in one readable phone view. No option label or commentary text outside the phone. Preserve app identity.

VARIANT 1: A clear, refined monthly prayer calendar, the best direct upgrade of the boxes. Activity card header serif gold "Prayer calendar", then "October 2026" with small left/right month arrows. Weekday labels M T W T F S S. Compact date cells in exactly 7 columns and 5 rows. October 2026 starts Thursday: row1 empty empty empty 1 2 3 4; row2 5 6 7 8 9 10 11; row3 12 13 14 15 16 17 18; row4 19 20 21 22 23 24 25; row5 26 27 28 29 30 31 empty. Use smaller softly rounded date squares compared to reference's huge empty boxes. Day9 filled gold with dark number9 and two tiny dark completion dots; day11 outlined gold, number11 cream. Days12-31 subdued as future dates, no fake activity. Thin low-key legend "Prayed" with gold dot and "Today" with gold outlined circle. Beneath grid a concise line "9 Oct · 2 rosaries" in readable type. Lower breakdown in elegant four text rows separated by hairlines with small gold totals. This option emphasizes date clarity, calm spacing and familiar calendar navigation.

VARIANT 2: A compact rosary-inspired activity grid using circular bead markers rather than large square boxes. Activity panel header gold serif "Recent days", subtitle "7 Sep – 11 Oct". Exactly35 circular day markers, seven per row. Inactive markers muted blue with a subtle interior highlight, like clean flat UI bead symbols, NOT 3D jewelry. A thin quiet connecting line horizontally across each row evokes rosary beads without visual clutter. Legend underneath "2 rosaries on 9 Oct" and a small outlined indicator labelled "Today". More compact than the current grid. Lower "By mystery set" shows four evenly spaced rows with slender horizontal track bars next to labels, Sorrowful filled gold ending number2, other rows empty blue tracks and0. Elegant app-native, devotional specificity, readable spacious layout.

edits.prompt: Edit this Cathopedia UI concept only in the lower 'By mystery set' panel: the Sorrowful bar must fill its ENTIRE blue track with gold, because all 2 of the 2 recorded rosaries are Sorrowful. Joyful, Glorious and Luminous remain completely empty blue tracks with number0. Keep Sorrowful number2. This is a distribution of completed prayers, not progress toward an invented goal. Preserve absolutely everything else: all text, bead grid, typography, colors, frame, sizing, layout and icons.
